settings.introHTML: This lesson teaches learners how to talk about family, friends, and relationships in French, describing relatives and using possessive adjectives correctly (for example mon frère, ma sœur, mes parents). It introduces the irregular verb avoir and common expressions that use it (for example j'ai faim, j'ai 25 ans). Learners also practise pronunciation of double ll (as in famille, fille, bouteille), developing accurate and natural speech when discussing family and personal relationships.
settings.informationHTML:
After completing this unit, you will be able to:

  • Talk about family members, friends, and neighbours in French.
  • Use possessive adjectives more accurately with singular and plural nouns.
  • Recognise and use common forms of avoir and everyday expressions built with it.
  • Improve listening comprehension through guided relationship and family-based tasks.
  • Recognise and produce the pronunciation patterns of French double ll more confidently.

dialogues.informationTextHTML: This section introduces short dialogues that show how to ask and answer questions about family, relatives, and relationships in French.

dialogues1.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: Tu as des frères et des sœurs ?
Have you got brothers and sisters?
Oui, j'ai un grand frère et deux petites sœurs. Et toi ?
Yes, I have a big (older) brother and two little (younger) sisters. What about you?
Je n'ai pas de frères, mais j'ai une sœur-jumelle.
I haven't got any brothers, but I've got a twin sister.
dialogues1.titleText: Informal questions about brothers and sisters

dialogues2.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: Vous avez des frères et des sœurs ?
Have you got brothers and sisters?
Non, je n'ai ni frères ni sœurs. Je suis enfant unique. Et vous ?
No, I've got neither brothers nor sisters. I'm an only child. What about you?
J'ai un demi-frère et une demi-sœur.
I've got a half-brother and a half-sister.
dialogues2.titleText: Formal questions about brothers and sisters

dialogues3.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: Caroline, do you have any children?
Ah non, nous n'avons pas d'enfants, pas encore ! Et vous ?
Oh no, we haven't got any children, not yet. What about you?
C'est un bébé. Il a cinq mois.
He's a baby. He's five months old.

vocabulary.informationTextHTML: This section introduces key family, relationship, and neighbour vocabulary used throughout the unit.

You will learn:

  • Core family vocabulary (for example frère, sœur, grands-parents).
  • Words for relationships and households (for example mari, femme, compagnon, voisin).
  • Useful ways to ask about age and family structure.
  • Vocabulary that supports the grammar, pronunciation, and exercise work in this unit.
phrases: Quel âge as-tu ? Tu as quel âge ?
Quel âge avez-vous ? Vous avez quel âge ?

grammar1.informationTextHTML: This section explains how possessive adjectives change according to noun gender and number in French.

grammar2.informationTextHTML: This section introduces the irregular verb avoir and some common expressions that use it.

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section introduces key grammar and usage for talking about family, relationships, and age in French, with a focus on possessive adjectives and the verb avoir.

pronunciation1.informationTextHTML: In this part, focus on cases where French double ll is pronounced like a clear l sound. Listen carefully and repeat each example aloud.

pronunciation2.informationTextHTML: Here, focus on words where double ll is pronounced like the English letter y. Listen, compare, and repeat.

pronunciation3.informationTextHTML: Finally, practise some common exception words where the spelling pattern does not follow the usual double ll rule.

selectExercise1.informationTextHTML: Play each audio clip and choose the French sentence that matches what you hear. Work through all items first, then use Check answers to review your choices. If needed, use Reset to try again, or Show answers to reveal the solutions.

items.text: [J'ai des sœurs.|*J'ai deux sœurs.|Je n'ai pas de sœurs.]
[Il a un frère.|*Elle a un frère.|Elles ont un frère.]
[Mon copain s'appelle David.|Mon conjoint s'appelle David.|*Mon compagnon s'appelle David.]
[*Ils ont un fils.|Ils ont deux fils.|Ils ont deux filles.]
[Mon amie est allemande.|Mes amis sont allemands.|*Mes amies sont allemandes.]

inlineChoiceGroup2.informationTextHTML: The following words all contain double ll. Listen to them carefully, and decide whether the double ll is pronounced y or l. Then use Check answers to review your choices. If needed, use Show answer to reveal the solutions and Reset to try again.

doubleLlPractice.informationTextHTML: Listen to La famille de Camille and Annabelle a une petite-fille, which contain lots of examples of double ll.

inlineChoiceGroup4.informationTextHTML: Read each sentence and choose the correct form of avoir. Work through all items first, then use Check answers to review your choices. If needed, use Show answer to reveal the correct forms, and Reset to try again.

items.text: Elle [ai|as|*a|avons|avez|ont] un fils de deux ans.
Ils [ai|as|a|avons|avez|*ont] un bébé de trois mois.

inlineChoiceGroup5.informationTextHTML: Read each sentence and choose the correct possessive adjective. Work through all items first, then use Check answers to review your choices. If needed, use Show answer to reveal the correct forms, and Reset to try again.

items.text: Louis n'est pas [*mon|ma|mes] frère. C'est [*mon|ma|mes] cousin.
Je vous présente [mon|*ma|mes] tante, Géraldine et [*mon|ma|mes] oncle, Simon.
Mélanie n'habite pas chez [*son|sa|ses] père, elle habite chez [son|*sa|ses] mère.
[*Notre|Nos] maison se trouve à cinq kilomètres d'ici.

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section gives you a chance to practise the key points from this unit. You will check your forms of avoir together with the correct possessive adjectives for family members, sharpen your pronunciation of double ll, and complete listening tasks about family relationships in French.
